concepts.why: The presence of a solitary, mobile, submucosal mass with ill-defined borders and a smooth mucosal surface, along with ultrasonography showing a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion, supports the diagnosis of an ectopic lymph node.
The clinical and radiographic findings, including a submucosal mass with a smooth mucosal surface and a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion on ultrasonography, are also consistent with a lipoma.
The presence of a diffuse extraoral swelling and a submucosal mass with ill-defined borders could also suggest a mucocele.
The clinical and radiographic findings, including a submucosal mass and a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion, could also be consistent with a dermoid cyst.
The presence of a submucosal mass and a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion could also suggest a vascular malformation.

rationales.F02: Pain is more commonly associated with vascular malformations and less with lipomas.
rationales.F04: A mobile submucosal mass is more typical of ectopic lymph nodes or lipomas.
rationales.F06: Ultrasonography showing a well-defined, hypoechoic lesion supports the diagnosis of an ectopic lymph node or lipoma.
rationales.F07: The provisional diagnosis directly mentions ectopic lymph node and lipoma as likely causes.
